NAME

md_docs_2windows-build-performance - Windows build performance

The native build keeps the Debug sanitizers enabled. Performance measurements should use the same sources, compiler, dependency SDK and build configuration, with other builds idle. A clean build with ccache disabled measures compilation; a clean build with a populated cache measures cache restoration. An unchanged Ninja invocation measures neither.

Build concurrency

On the Ryzen 7 5800X workstation, clean native builds took 89.1 seconds with eight jobs, 97.0 seconds with twelve, and 107.0 seconds with sixteen. These are individual measurements, not a guarantee for other machines or workloads.

Windows Ninja builds default to a compile pool matching physical cores when there is no explicit parallelism setting. An existing CMAKE_BUILD_PARALLEL_LEVEL or CMAKE_JOB_POOL_COMPILE setting is respected. Configure-time environment changes do not persist into a later terminal process; the Ninja pool does.

For this workstation, use cmake --Build System Build System --target ascii-chat --parallel 8. To persist that limit in an existing build directory with a different global environment setting, configure with:

cmake --preset default -B build `


  -DCMAKE_JOB_POOLS=asciichat_compile=8 `


  -DCMAKE_JOB_POOL_COMPILE=asciichat_compile

Unity builds

cmake --preset windows-unity -B build
cmake --build build --target ascii-chat --parallel 8

This is a sanitized Debug build. On Windows the unity option batches project library sources as well as application mode sources. Vendored sources stay separate so DLL export filtering retains their source paths. Library batches contain four files; the executable uses CMake's normal batch size.

The first unity experiment took 72.7 seconds versus 89.1 seconds without unity. Rebuilding an individual source can require recompiling its batch, and source name or macro conflicts can arise as code changes. Ordinary development builds therefore keep unity disabled by default. Switch back with:

cmake --preset default -B build -DASCIICHAT_ENABLE_UNITY_BUILDS=OFF

Export generation and headers

DLL export generation scans all active object files in one llvm-nm invocation using a response file. PCH files and vendored objects are excluded, filename headings are discarded, and extraction failures stop the build. Bulk filtering and one output write avoid per-symbol file operations. A comparison of the same 338 manifest entries produced the same 2,694 exports in 0.39 seconds instead of 27.5 seconds.

Clang time traces showed roughly 0.8–1 second of Windows-header parsing in sampled audio, crypto and application C sources without PCH. Existing PCH coverage made that cost much smaller in covered sources. Extending PCH to more modules created a C++ macro conflict; a C-only variant compiled, but its full build took 104.2 seconds and did not demonstrate a benefit. The existing coverage was retained.

Later validation builds overlapped unrelated workstation workloads, so their wall-clock times should not be treated as a controlled speed comparison.

Compiler cache

Native launchers pass max_size=12G Compression Module=true compression_level=1 directly to ccache when its installed version supports configuration arguments. PCH targets also pass sloppiness=pch_defines,time_macros and Clang's -fno-pch-timestamp. This avoids launching one or two extra CMake processes per source file. Older ccache versions retain the environment-launcher fallback; the Emscripten compiler wrapper remains unchanged.

A full native unity build with an isolated empty cache took 90.9 seconds. After cleaning all objects and rebuilding, all 211 compiler calls were direct cache hits with zero misses, and the build took 18.2 seconds. This includes restoring objects, regenerating exports and linking; it is not an unchanged-build timing. These two runs also switch from the old environment launchers to the direct native launchers, so their timing combines cache hits and launcher savings.

The C/C++ PCH regression and Windows export tests can be run separately from Criterion:

uv run --project tests/ascii_chat_tests --frozen python -m pytest tests/python/cmake/test_ccache_pch.py
uv run --project tests/ascii_chat_tests --frozen python -m pytest tests/python/cmake/test_windows_exports.py
